# FSx for ONTAP Agentic Access-Aware RAG

> A deployable AWS CDK implementation of permission-aware RAG over Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP.
> Documents are reached through an FSx for ONTAP S3 Access Point; per-document permission metadata
> is kept in a separate index and matched against the user's SID / UID / GID **at query time**,
> after retrieval. The original NTFS ACLs are not carried through the S3 Access Point path, so the
> permission index is maintained separately rather than projected from the ACLs.

This repository is the implementation and measurement side. For lifecycle- and topic-organized
guidance on adopting FSx for ONTAP (assess → design → migrate → build → operate → optimize), see
the [FSx for ONTAP Adoption Playbook](https://github.com/Yoshiki0705/FSx-for-ONTAP-Adoption-Playbook).
Content is not duplicated between the two: guidance lives there, running code and measurements live
here.

## How to read this repository

Claims about how a product or service behaves carry an inline evidence label. The four tiers are
shared with the Adoption Playbook, so the same word means the same thing in both repositories.

- `verified` — reproduced by the author; the label carries the date and the Region.
- `documented` — stated in AWS or NetApp documentation; a source accompanies it.
- `field-observation` — observed once, reproduction not confirmed. Not a general rule.
- `hypothesis` — reasoned but unverified. Not a basis for a design decision.

Do not present `field-observation` or `hypothesis` content as established fact. A number is only
meaningful together with the date, Region, and configuration stated next to it. Two distinctions
matter throughout: a sample run is not a production estimate, and **code existing in this repository
does not mean it is deployed** — some modules are present but referenced by no stack.

Definition and enforcement: [Evidence Policy](docs/en/evidence-policy.md), checked by
`scripts/check-evidence.py`.

Naming: "Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP" on first mention, "FSx for ONTAP" thereafter.

## Entry points

- [README (Japanese)](README.md) — primary hub: architecture, feature flags, deployment.
- [README (English)](README.en.md) — same structure in English.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) — conventions, build and test commands, feature flags, and the pitfalls
  table for coding agents. Read this before changing code.
- [Evidence Policy](docs/en/evidence-policy.md) — the four tiers, their required metadata, and what
  they do not answer.
- [Permission Metadata Consistency Model](docs/en/permission-consistency.md) — how permission data
  propagates, where it is fail-closed, and what it never reaches. Read this before relying on the
  permission boundary.
- [Threat Model](docs/en/threat-model.md) — threat categories, attack paths, and the preconditions
  each mitigation depends on.
- [SID Filtering Architecture](docs/en/SID-Filtering-Architecture.md) — how retrieved chunks are
  matched against the caller's identity.
- [S3 AP + AD Prerequisites](docs/en/s3ap-ad-prerequisites.md) — verified constraints when the SVM
  is joined to Active Directory, including why `HeadBucket` succeeds while data operations fail.
- [Stack Architecture Comparison](docs/en/stack-architecture-comparison.md) — vector store and
  deployment variants.

## Running the checks

`make help` lists every check. The same commands run in CI.

- `make all` — the fast checks: type check, Jest tests, documentation links, evidence labels,
  dependency severity policy.
- `make synth` — `cdk synth` across the ten feature-flag combinations. The flags are read from
  `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml` so the two cannot drift apart.
- `make secrets` / `make actions` — gitleaks and zizmor.

Each detector runs its own `--selftest` before the real check: a gate passing is not evidence that
the gate ran.

## Languages

Documentation is written in Japanese first and mirrored in English; six further languages (ko,
zh-CN, zh-TW, fr, de, es) exist under `docs/<lang>/` with partial coverage. Japanese and English are
kept in structural parity. Where a translation is absent the link points at the English version
rather than a placeholder.

## What is here

- `bin/`, `lib/` — CDK application and stacks (networking, security, storage, AI, web app,
  Transfer Family, embedding).
- `docker/nextjs/` — Next.js 15 frontend running on Lambda; permission filtering, smart routing,
  and the chat surface.
- `lambda/`, `automation/` — Python and TypeScript functions: KB auto-sync, FSx for ONTAP
  operations, Transfer Family ingestion.
- `tests/` — CDK assertions and property-based tests; `tests/permission-matrix/` holds the
  permission scenarios.
- `benchmarks/` — measurement scripts and recorded results. Read the evidence label before quoting
  a number.
- `docs/` — design, operations, and investigation documents in up to eight languages.

## What is not here

- Guidance on choosing or migrating to FSx for ONTAP. That is the Adoption Playbook's scope.
- A production-ready deployment. This is a demonstration: removal policies are destructive, and
  several capabilities are opt-in behind feature flags precisely because they are unverified.
